findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the open-ended 'Review of every new test confirms...' AC with a concrete, deterministic criterion — e.g., 'No new test asserts on private attributes, internal module paths, or raw source text; verified by CI (e.g., a linter rule or structural test-review checklist that produces a pass/fail artifact)' — or fold this constraint into the test-design prose and drop it as a standalone AC.
evidence: 'Review of every new test confirms it asserts observable behavior, serialized/public contracts, or persisted state; none greps source text or asserts private implementation shape'

No proving command (e.g. a test name, a CI check, a structured assertion) is given that would mechanically confirm this property — the word 'review' implies human judgment, not a deterministic evaluation.
F1 requires a specific observable outcome and in-session evaluability; this AC is evaluable only by subjective inspection.
findings.finding: The AC 'Review of every new test confirms it asserts observable behavior, serialized/public contracts, or persisted state; none greps source text or asserts private implementation shape' is effort/process-framed ('review of every new test') and has no concrete proving command — it describes a human review action rather than a specific observable, deterministic outcome.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'Review of every new test confirms it asserts observable behavior...'
scenarios: An executor adds tests that grep source text; CI stays green; the AC appears satisfied because no automated check catches the violation.
A reviewer disagrees on what 'private implementation shape' means; the AC is argued rather than measured.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove this item from the formal AC list (it is already covered by the Test Design prose 'Tests assert observable behavior and public contracts, never grep source text or depend on private implementation shape') and instead add a short CI-checkable rule — e.g., a custom pylint/flake8 plugin or an agreed naming convention — that makes the constraint mechanical. If no automation is feasible, state the reviewing convention explicitly and mark the criterion [operator-attested].

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the `_chunk` extra-context injection in `pass1.py` compositional: accumulate all per-criterion extra blocks for the chunk and concatenate them, rather than replacing with a single criterion's block.
evidence: Plan: 'Extend that branch explicitly with any(c.get("id") == "no-file-impact" for c in chunk)'
Existing code: `extra = decomp_context if any(c.get('id') == 'G5' for c in chunk) else ''` — single string, not compositional
plan_review_G5.md front matter: `dimension: scope-intent`; plan specifies `no-file-impact` with facet `scope-intent` — same facet → same chunk under `chunk_by_facet`
Both criteria active simultaneously when ticket has file_impact_scope == 'none' (no suppress for G5)
findings.finding: The `_chunk` closure in `pass1.py` passes a single `extra` string to `_pass1_with_ladder`. The plan extends the G5-only branch to also handle `no-file-impact`, but does not specify that the two extra-context strings must be concatenated when both G5 and `no-file-impact` land in the same facet chunk. Both criteria share `facet: scope-intent` (confirmed from existing prompt files), so on a `file_impact_scope == 'none'` ticket they will co-chunk. The plan's proposed branch — `extra = decomp_context if any(G5) else ''` extended with `any(no-file-impact)` — results in a mutual-exclusion pattern that loses one context block when both criteria are co-chunked.
scenarios: A ticket with `file_impact_scope: none` and children (or G5-applicable content) has both G5 and `no-file-impact` in the same `scope-intent` chunk. The `_chunk` closure either injects the decomp_context (G5 wins) or the declared-reason block (no-file-impact wins), but not both. The losing criterion runs without its required extra context.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the single-winner pattern with: `extras = [decomp_context] if any(c.get('id') == 'G5' for c in chunk) else []; if any(c.get('id') == 'no-file-impact' for c in chunk): extras.append(<declared_reason_block>); extra = '\n\n'.join(e for e in extras if e)`

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in the `pass1.py` extension how `decomp_context` and the `declared_reason` block are combined when a chunk contains both G5 and `no-file-impact` (e.g. concatenated as separate Markdown sections, with ordering defined), so neither context is silently dropped in the co-occurrence case.
evidence: Plan text: 'facet scope-intent' for no-file-impact
criteria_routing.json: G5 also has 'facet: scope-intent'
pass1.py line 418: 'extra = decomp_context if any(c.get("id") == "G5" for c in chunk) else ""' — single string
Plan text: 'Extend that branch explicitly with any(c.get("id") == "no-file-impact" for c in chunk)' — no merge/concatenation semantics specified
ABSENCE: no specification of how decomp_context and declared_reason are combined when a chunk contains both G5 and no-file-impact
findings.finding: The plan assigns `no-file-impact` to `facet: scope-intent`, the same facet as G5. `chunk_by_facet()` packs same-facet 1-TURN criteria together, so when a ticket has `file_impact_scope: none` AND children, both G5 and `no-file-impact` land in the same chunk. `pass1.py`'s `_chunk()` uses a single `extra_context: str` parameter. The plan extends the branch with `any(c.get('id') == 'no-file-impact' for c in chunk)` but does not specify how `decomp_context` (the G5 injection) and the `declared_reason` block (the `no-file-impact` injection) are combined when both criteria co-reside in a chunk. The naive if/elif extension supplies only one context string, silently dropping the other.
findings.location: Declared-reason data flow section; `pass1.py` `_chunk()` function (line 418 in current codebase)
scenarios: A container ticket (has children) with file_impact_scope:none and a non-empty no_file_impact_reason triggers both G5 (non-empty decomp_context) and no-file-impact. chunk_by_facet() places them in the same scope-intent chunk. The extended _chunk() conditional must choose one context string; whichever branch fires first wins and the other context is silently dropped, causing either the decomposition state to be invisible to G5 or the declared reason to be invisible to no-file-impact.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the `_chunk` extra-context logic to build `extra` by concatenating all applicable context blocks: `extra = '\n\n'.join(filter(None, [decomp_context if any G5 else '', declared_reason_block if any no-file-impact else '']))`. This is order-stable and additive, so the G5 and no-file-impact paths both get their required context. Document the concatenation order (decomp first, declared-reason second) so the prompt structure is reproducible.

findings.finding: AC 17 mixes an in-session-verifiable constraint ('no source-grep/change-detector tests are added') with a forward-looking design principle ('remain green under behavior-preserving refactors') that cannot be verified within the session. An agent completing this work has no deterministic in-session command that proves the forward-looking part; it is guidance, not a measurable criterion.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'New tests are behavior/contract-focused and remain green under behavior-preserving refactors; no source-grep/change-detector tests are added.'
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the single AC with: (a) '[ ] No new test uses source-file grep, internal symbol name matching, or change-detector assertions — confirmed by code review of added test files.' and move 'remain green under behavior-preserving refactors' to the Test Design section as an authoring guideline rather than an acceptance criterion.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Expand `reason_grounded` from `yes|no` to `yes|no|insufficient` so the model can signal 'reason present but too vague/unverifiable to classify as grounded or contradicted', enabling the `assertion_plausible: insufficient` branch to be reachable via the sub-answer logic.
evidence: Plan text: 'reason_grounded: yes|no' (binary, no insufficient option)
Plan text: 'Set assertion_plausible: insufficient when reason_grounded: no, repo_file_change_named: no, and the plan is too vague to establish either outcome'
plan_review_necessity.md: 'demonstrates_necessity {yes|no|insufficient}' — same pattern, three-way vocabulary for sub-answer that can be vague
plan_review_asserted_capability.md: 'asserted_capability_grounded {yes|no|insufficient}' — identical pattern
ABSENCE: no third value on reason_grounded to express 'cannot determine groundedness from the available plan text'
findings.finding: The `reason_grounded` sub-answer is defined as binary {yes|no}, but the decision rule for `assertion_plausible: insufficient` requires distinguishing 'reason is too vague to evaluate' from 'reason is present but clearly ungrounded/contradicted' — both would map to `reason_grounded: no`, collapsing two semantically distinct states that drive different criterion outcomes (fire a contradiction finding vs. return non-blocking coaching). The model cannot deterministically route to `assertion_plausible: insufficient` via the sub-answers alone because there is no third value on `reason_grounded` to signal 'ambiguous/insufficient evidence.' Every comparable criterion in the codebase (necessity, asserted-capability, decomp-shape, removal-rationale) uses `{yes|no|insufficient}` on sub-answers precisely where vagueness is an expected case.
findings.location: Criterion judgment and prompt discovery — CHECKLIST SUB-ANSWERS definition; `reason_grounded: yes|no`
scenarios: A ticket declares file_impact_scope:none with a reason like 'this change only affects runtime behavior'. The model judges: no repo file change named, reason present but neither clearly grounded nor clearly fabricated (insufficient evidence). It must set reason_grounded:no (the only option available), which the decision rule maps to assertion_plausible:no → fires a contradiction finding. But the correct output is assertion_plausible:insufficient → coaching. The binary vocabulary forces the wrong outcome.

Equivalently: a ticket with a highly specific, credible reason gets reason_grounded:yes → assertion_plausible:yes even if a repo file change is also implied — the binary yes/no on reason_grounded makes the insufficient path unreachable from the sub-answers.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the sub-answer declaration to: `reason_grounded: yes|no|insufficient` — `yes` when the reason names a concrete external deliverable or explicit architectural constraint that explains why no file changes occur; `no` when the reason contradicts the plan or is demonstrably absent; `insufficient` when the plan has a reason but it is too vague to verify either way. Update the decision rule: `assertion_plausible: insufficient` fires when `reason_grounded: insufficient` (regardless of repo_file_change_named, as long as it is `no`).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify (or confirm the existing framework specifies) the fallback behavior when the LLM sub-answer for `no-file-impact` contains missing, null, or out-of-enum values — the plan should state that any parse/validation failure falls through to fail-open (no finding emitted, criterion skipped) rather than raising or mis-classifying.
evidence: Plan defines decision rules for yes/no/insufficient but has no catch-all for unexpected/malformed LLM sub-answer values
Plan states 'existing advisory Pass-1 framework already owns LLM execution and fail-open behavior' but does not confirm that sub-answer schema violations are covered by that fail-open path

The three-field co-located sub-answer contract (assertion_plausible, reason_grounded, repo_file_change_named) introduces new structured-output parsing that could produce values outside the enumerated set
findings.finding: The plan's decision rules enumerate exactly three `assertion_plausible` outcomes (yes/no/insufficient) and rely on the existing framework's fail-open behavior, but do not specify what the criterion emits when the LLM returns a malformed sub-answer response (e.g., missing field, unexpected enum value, or unparseable structured output). If the existing framework's fail-open path does not cover per-criterion sub-answer schema violations, this new failure point could silently mis-classify or raise an unhandled exception rather than producing a safe no-finding result.
findings.location: Approach — 'Criterion judgment and prompt discovery' / decision rules section
scenarios: LLM returns a response where assertion_plausible is absent or misspelled — criterion raises KeyError or AttributeError instead of failing open
LLM returns an unexpected enum value (e.g., 'unclear') not covered by the three decision rules — the criterion silently falls through without emitting any finding, masking a real contradiction
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the decision rules: 'If any sub-answer field is absent or holds an unrecognised value, treat the response as unparseable and apply the existing fail-open path (no finding emitted for this criterion).'. This closes the gap without bespoke machinery.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document in the `pass1.py` `_chunk` closure extension that the `extra`-context branches for G5 and `no-file-impact` are mutually exclusive BY FACET (G5 is `decomp-signal`, `no-file-impact` is `scope-intent`) and assert or note that co-chunking these two criteria must never occur — or alternatively adopt the more general `{criterion_id: extra_context}` dict pattern that `_chunk` iterates, making the composition explicit and collision-safe.
evidence: Plan says: 'Extend that branch explicitly with `any(c.get("id") == "no-file-impact" for c in chunk)` so a matching chunk receives this exact Markdown section'
pass1.py line 418: `extra = decomp_context if any(c.get('id') == 'G5' for c in chunk) else ''` — single `extra` string, one branch wins
criteria_routing.json: G5 uses facet `decomp-signal`; plan specifies `no-file-impact` uses facet `scope-intent` — so they never co-chunk today, but this constraint is unspecified in the plan
ABSENCE: the plan contains no statement that the facet difference is the load-bearing guarantee of non-collision
findings.finding: The plan extends `pass1.py`'s `_chunk` closure with a second inline `extra`-context branch (`any(c.get('id') == 'no-file-impact' for c in chunk)`) alongside the existing G5 branch, but does not document the implicit assumption that makes this safe: G5 and `no-file-impact` use different facets (`decomp` vs `scope-intent`) and are therefore guaranteed never to share a chunk. If this facet-separation invariant were ever violated, both branches would conflict over the single `extra` string — one would silently win and the other's context would be dropped, producing a subtly incorrect prompt with no error.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Declared-reason data flow'; pass1.py `_chunk` closure (line 418)
scenarios: A future refactor consolidates or renames facets, placing G5 and `no-file-impact` in the same chunk — both branches fire, one context silently overwrites the other, producing a subtly wrong prompt.
A reviewer implementing from the plan does not realize the single-`extra` pattern only works when the two criteria cannot co-chunk, and extracts a different facet assignment.
findings.suggested_fix: In the plan's 'Declared-reason data flow' section, add a sentence: 'Because G5 uses facet `decomp-signal` and `no-file-impact` uses facet `scope-intent`, the two extra-context injections are never co-chunked and the single `extra` string in `_chunk` is correct. Add a comment in `pass1.py` capturing this constraint.' Alternatively, generalize `extra` to a `dict[str, str]` keyed by criterion ID so future additions are composable.

findings.finding: `reason_grounded` and `repo_file_change_named` are declared as CHECKLIST SUB-ANSWER fields in the criterion schema but their roles in the decision protocol are never specified anywhere in the plan. The three decision rules branch exclusively on `assertion_plausible`; neither `reason_grounded` nor `repo_file_change_named` appears in any rule, coaching instruction, or output contract. An executor filling these fields has no protocol for how the values affect the criterion's output.
findings.location: Plan section 'Criterion judgment and prompt discovery' — CHECKLIST SUB-ANSWERS definition and decision rules
findings.suggested_fix: If the intended semantics are: `repo_file_change_named: yes` overrides `insufficient` to `no` (a named file change is a plausibility signal strong enough to fire), add that rule explicitly. If `reason_grounded: no` tightens the `insufficient` coaching, state that. Otherwise remove the orphaned fields.
